how: Curling Hong Kong China runs a Learn to Curl programme on converted shopping-centre ice rinks such as Festival Walk, plus ice-free floor curling at The Ball Room in Kwun Tong.
venue: Curling Hong Kong China / Hong Kong Curling Academy

how: The Hong Kong GAA club plays Gaelic football, hurling and camogie, welcomes all ages and nationalities, and has hosted the Asian Gaelic Games at King's Park.
The Hong Kong Dragons Australian rules club trains at the Hong Kong Rugby Club and competes in the South China AFL; junior Auskick runs alongside.
The Hong Kong, China Lacrosse Association supports clubs, and beginner lacrosse classes run on a covered court in Kai Tak with stick rental.
venue: Hong Kong, China Lacrosse Association / Crossealley Sports

how: The Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club runs outrigger canoe introduction courses and adult open days from Middle Island in Deep Water Bay.
venue: Royal Hong Kong Yacht Club (Middle Island)

how: Free flight in Hong Kong is mainly paragliding, taught by local associations and clubs (about 200 people join per year), from a small number of permitted hill take-off sites; true hang gliding is rare.

how: Indoor airsoft arenas such as War Zone in Lai Chi Kok and Tact Zone in Quarry Bay offer CQB games and a 35 m range; airsoft guns are legal under 2 joules.
Paintball Headquarters in Kowloon Bay has a 10,000 sq ft indoor field, and outdoor war-game sites operate in Tuen Mun for groups.
Cosmic Dance, founded in 2009 by a Kalakshetra-trained teacher, teaches Bharatanatyam in Hong Kong, mostly in small private groups.
Sri Shakti Academy is listed as a classical Indian dance school teaching Kathak to adults.
Toki Studio in Quarry Bay runs beginner clay courses covering hand-building and wheel throwing, and Lantau Pottery Studio in Mui Wo and Under The Stone in Kowloon offer hand-building sessions.
Waka Artisans taught kintsugi courses (starter pack of three classes with tools and materials) at PMQ in Central; listings date from 2017 to 2020 so current schedules need checking.
Hong Kong Open Printshop, an artist-run non-profit print studio in Shek Kip Mei, runs screen-printing workshops, and the HKU University Museum has run small screen-printing classes.
The Hong Kong Philatelic Society, founded in 1921 with over 350 members, holds exhibitions and publishes a journal and newsletters for stamp collectors.
Hong Kong Sign Language beginner courses run through CUHK (HKSL1001), PolyU continuing education taught by Sign Language Communication Office (龍耳), and one-off experiential workshops.
venue: PolyU continuing education (Sign Language - Elementary Level)

how: The Hong Kong Parkour Association offers weekly open sessions and group training, Trybe in Kennedy Town runs classes, and beginner workshops are listed by Time Out.
Hong Kong has an active breaking scene including the UTLR852 Breaking Club, but no specific beginner class listing was found.
Ikebana International Hong Kong Chapter (founded 1959) and the Ikenobo Hong Kong Chapter run ikebana study groups, workshops and a booth at the Hong Kong Flower Show.
venue: Ikebana International Hong Kong Chapter / Ikenobo Hong Kong Chapter

how: Hong Kong Kiteboarding School teaches beginner kitesurfing lessons at Pui O Beach or Shui Hau Wan on Lantau depending on season.

Towed water sports are available as wakeboarding and wakesurfing (Hong Kong Wakeboard at Tai Tam Tuk, Wake Plus and Wake2Chill in Sai Kung), and a local association promotes waterskiing and wakeboarding, but dedicated water-ski lessons were not confirmed.
Hong Kong Amateur Orchestra (about 40 members, formed 2007) and the Hong Kong Youth Music Society's Chinese orchestra hold weekly practices and accept adult amateur players.
The Hong Kong Polo Team and Hong Kong Polo Development, founded in 2018 to widen access, play and teach polo, with a Sai Kung facility.
The Malt & Grain Whisk(e)y Society Hong Kong is a non-profit whisky appreciation society, and the Scotch Malt Whisky Society has a Hong Kong branch.
venue: Malt & Grain Whisk(e)y Society Hong Kong

how: One-off beer and sake fermentation workshops run at PMQ, led by founders of Sunday Sake and Young Master Brewery, and sake masterclasses are held at the Hong Kong Sake Festival.
venue: PMQ beer and sake fermentation workshop

how: Global Game Jam Hong Kong is held annually at Cyberport (over 400 participants in 2019, run with PolyU), and universities such as HKU run VR game jams.
venue: Global Game Jam Hong Kong at Cyberport

how: Hackathons are held periodically in Hong Kong, such as the 12-hour Global Hackathon launch event during Hong Kong Blockchain Week, alongside university and Cyberport events.
venue: Cyberport / Hong Kong Blockchain Week events

how: Over 200 butterfly species are recorded in Hong Kong; GreenPower publishes butterfly trails (Shing Mun, Tai Po Kau, The Peak) and the Hong Kong Lepidopterists' Society runs field trips and talks.
venue: Shing Mun Butterfly Garden / Hong Kong Lepidopterists' Society

how: Enhale Meditation Studio in Central offers drop-in and credit-based classes daily, and the Kadampa Meditation Centre in Sheung Wan runs drop-in meditation classes open to non-Buddhists.
Numerous pilates studios operate in Central, such as U One Studio and One Pilates Studio, with reformer and mat classes bookable through ClassPass.
World Snooker Club 147 in Sheung Wan has 30 tables, and licensed snooker and pool halls are found across the territory, with local tournaments run by the Billiard Sports Council of Hong Kong China.
Veteran magician Harry Wong Cher-hong has run workshops open to the public, though a local report notes no registered institutions teach magic and most magicians are self-taught.
Pedal boats can be rented at the Wong Nai Chung Reservoir Park kiosk (two- and four-seaters with lifejackets) and at the Water Sports and Recreation Precinct in Wan Chai.
The Hong Kong Chess Federation runs the annual FIDE-rated Hong Kong Open Championship at Smithfield Sports Centre in Kennedy Town, plus other adult and junior events.
venue: Hong Kong Chess Federation (Smithfield Sports Centre)

how: Yarn in the Works offers beginner knitting and crochet classes with regular knit nights, and Pinkoi-listed studios in Tsuen Wan and Kwai Chung run one-off crochet workshops.
The Mills in Tsuen Wan hosts textile programmes including an annual Weaving Festival with weaving and crochet workshops, but regular frame-loom classes were not confirmed.

Chiuchow (Teochew) opera in Hong Kong has declined and is mainly staged in temporary theatres during the Bon Festival in districts with large Chiuchow communities, such as Shau Kei Wan and Kowloon City.
The free Hong Kong Railway Museum in the former Tai Po Market station displays historic locomotives and coaches, while live rail watching is possible from MTR and KCR lines.
Fa Yuen Street in Mong Kok, known as Sneaker Street, has more than fifty sports-shoe stores open daily until about 22:30.
The Hong Kong Heritage Museum in Sha Tin holds Cantonese opera and local culture collections, with branch sites such as the Sheung Yiu Folk Museum in a former Hakka village.
The Hong Kong Amateur Radio Transmitting Society (HARTS) is a hobbyist radio group running events and covering the tiers of operating permits.
venue: Hong Kong Amateur Radio Transmitting Society

how: Hong Kong UNESCO Global Geopark sites (Ma Shi Chau, Lai Chi Chong, Tung Ping Chau, Port Island) show fossils and distinctive rocks for observation, but the collecting rules were not confirmed.
area: Sai Kung / Tolo Channel / Tung Ping Chau

how: The Hong Kong Archaeological Society (membership-based) has carried out excavations such as Mong Tseng Wai and Luk Keng Village; public participation depends on membership.
